section_style_guide.purpose: Provide decision-useful, IFRS-aligned disclosure of sustainability- and climate-related metrics and targets, including definitions, reporting-period values, methodologies, boundaries, limitations, and traceability to sources and related narrative elsewhere in the report.
section_style_guide.tone: Formal, standards-led, neutral and audit-ready. Emphasize clarity, completeness, transparency, and accountability. Use forward-looking language cautiously for planned enhancements (state intent and progress, avoid guarantees). Keep performance commentary minimal; prioritize definitional and methodological precision.
section_style_guide.level_of_detail: High detail in structured tables (definitions, values, sources, mappings). Brief narrative lead-in to set scope and governance expectations. Provide sufficient methodological detail to enable comparability and assurance readiness, using footnotes and structured bullets rather than long prose.
section_style_guide.paragraph_style: Start with a short contextual overview explaining why metrics/targets are disclosed and what they enable users to assess. Clearly separate general sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) from climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2). Include an approach paragraph on metric selection (relevance/materiality lens) and target-setting principles. Add a methodology/transparency paragraph covering boundaries, data collection, estimation, and changes over time. End the narrative lead-in with a data currency statement and update cadence/location statement before presenting tables. Where complex metrics require explanation, use a structured sequence: boundary → inputs/sources → calculation steps → outputs/uses → limitations → governance/controls.
section_style_guide.sentence_style: Short, precise, technical sentences. Prefer definitional constructions (e.g., “Metric is defined as…”, “Includes…/Excludes…”, “Calculated using…”). Use parallel phrasing in lists. Use explicit status statements for unavailable items (do not leave blanks). Avoid promotional adjectives and unqualified claims.
section_style_guide.preferred_evidence_style: Traceability-first. For each metric/target, provide (a) external framework/source type reference where applicable, (b) internal source location/document reference (generic descriptor), and (c) mapping to related report section/pillar. Use structured definitions and boundary statements to reduce ambiguity. Indicate assurance coverage at the data-point level via a symbol/marker with a consolidated legend and assurance scope note.
section_style_guide.table_usage: Primary disclosure vehicle is a multi-page metrics register with a fixed, repeated column structure. Support mixed data types (numeric, qualitative, zero values, and ‘not reported/not applicable’ statements). Allow multi-line cells, bullets, and sub-parts within definitions and values. Use nested mini-tables inside cells for disaggregation breakdowns and include an explicit total row. Repeat table headers on each page; maintain consistent column widths and alignment (labels left, numbers right).
section_style_guide.figure_usage: Optional and secondary to tables. Use figures only to clarify distribution or boundary reconciliation when helpful (e.g., category distribution; reconciliation/step-down of reporting perimeter). Keep figure titles and terminology consistent with tables and narrative. Avoid decorative charts; prioritize explanatory visuals.
section_style_guide.pdf_layout_usage: Use a clear chapter/section opener and consistent running headers/footers with section label and page numbering (generic report identifier only). Separate narrative lead-in from table blocks with whitespace. Tables should span full width with controlled wrapping. Place footnotes and assurance legend consistently near the relevant content or as a consolidated note at the end of the table segment. Visually separate results, boundary/reconciliation, assurance note, and methodology blocks.
section_style_guide.how_to_discuss_missing_data: State availability explicitly (e.g., not reported for the period, not applicable, under development). Provide a brief reason category (data availability, methodological maturity, boundary constraints) and describe the planned improvement direction without committing to outcomes or timelines. Use consistent placeholders and avoid leaving cells blank.
what_to_avoid: Any organization-specific names, branded footers, report identifiers, or unique labels
Any person names, role titles that could identify a specific organization, or committee names
Any numeric values, targets, dates, time horizons, currencies, percentages, totals, or thresholds in reusable templates
Any exact metric lists, metric wording, or topic mappings that reflect a specific entity’s material topics
Any vendor/tool/provider names or proprietary methodologies presented as fixed requirements
Any jurisdiction-specific regulatory program references tied to a particular regulator or country
Any unqualified claims of compliance, leadership, ambition, or stakeholder outcomes
Any assurance provider identity or verbatim assurance standard citations as fixed text
Overly persuasive storytelling; keep commentary minimal and evidence-led

recommended_tables.purpose: Serve as the primary disclosure index/register with definitions, values, and traceability metadata.
suggested_columns: Mapping to report section/pillar (governance/strategy/risk management/metrics and targets)
formatting_rules: Repeat header row on each page
Use explicit placeholders for not applicable/not reported
Use consistent unit notation in headers or value cells (do not mix styles)

recommended_tables.purpose: Provide category-by-category breakdowns for selected metrics within the register or as a standalone table.
formatting_rules: Keep category taxonomy generic and entity-defined
Use consistent ordering and definitions across periods

recommended_tables.purpose: Explain reporting perimeter using a reconciliation structure (starting population → exclusions → final scope).
suggested_columns: Resulting perimeter/status (qualitative or quantitative, as applicable)
formatting_rules: Cross-reference to methodology notes/footnotes for detailed rules

recommended_tables.table_name: Assurance Marker Legend and Scope Summary
recommended_tables.purpose: Explain assurance markers used in tables and summarize assurance scope at a high level.
suggested_columns: Where to find the full assurance statement (generic reference)
formatting_rules: Use one consolidated legend per section
Do not embed provider names in the template

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Visualize the step-down from starting population to final reporting scope and optional breakdown.
design_notes: Flow/step-down structure: start → exclusions → final scope → optional category split
Use terminology consistent with the reconciliation table

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Show distribution of a selected metric across categories when it improves interpretability.
design_notes: Mirror category labels used in the disaggregation table
Avoid clutter; prioritize clarity over aesthetics

contents: One-paragraph purpose and IFRS basis statement
Approach to metric selection and target setting
Data currency and update cadence statement
Comparability notes and change log references

recommended_pdf_blocks.block_name: Assurance legend and scope note block
Methodology appendix-style block (within section or cross-referenced)

required_narrative_blocks: Purpose and IFRS basis: explain that metrics and targets are disclosed to support user assessment and align with IFRS S1/S2 requirements.
Scope separation: clearly distinguish general sustainability metrics from climate-related metrics and targets.
Selection and target-setting approach: describe how metrics are chosen (relevance/materiality) and how targets are set and monitored (measurable, time-bound where applicable).
Boundary and methodology overview: define reporting boundary, inclusions/exclusions, key assumptions, estimation methods, and uncertainty considerations.
Data governance and controls: describe ownership, review/approval controls, and change management for methodologies and metrics.
Data currency and update cadence: state the snapshot timing conceptually and where/when updates are provided (without specific dates in the template).
Missing data protocol: explain how unavailable metrics are labeled and how improvement plans are communicated cautiously.
optional_narrative_blocks: Alignment bridge: brief note on alignment/mapping to other commonly used frameworks (generic reference only).
Comparability and restatements: explain changes in definitions, boundaries, or methodologies and how comparatives are treated.
Decision-usefulness note: short explanation of how management uses key metrics/targets in decision-making (without performance claims).
Granularity pathway: principle-based statement on potential future disaggregation as data quality improves.
output_structure_rules: Keep narrative concise; place most disclosure content in structured tables.
Use consistent subsection numbering and short functional headings.
Present IFRS S1-aligned and IFRS S2-aligned disclosures in clearly separated blocks (adjacent but distinct).
Ensure every metric row includes: definition, value/status, source type, internal source location, and mapping to report section/pillar.
Do not leave blanks in value fields; use standardized status labels for missing/not applicable items.
Use footnotes for methodological conventions and edge-case rules; avoid burying critical definitions in footnotes.
If assurance markers are used, apply them consistently and explain them once in a consolidated legend with scope/limitations.
For disaggregations, include totals and define category taxonomy; keep taxonomy stable across periods or explain changes.
Maintain consistent units and formatting across tables; avoid mixing unit presentation styles.
Include a brief change-management note when definitions/methodologies change (what changed, why, and comparability impact).

section_specific_no_copying_rules: Do not reuse any specific metric names, definitions, or mappings from any reference report; create an entity-specific metric set based on the new entity’s material topics and IFRS requirements.
Do not reuse any sector/category lists, classification systems, or ordering from any reference report; define categories appropriate to the new entity and explain them.
Do not reuse any assurance symbols, legends, or wording verbatim; adapt to the new report’s assurance approach and terminology.
Do not include any internal document titles, system names, vendor names, or website links from any reference report; use generic placeholders for internal source locations and external references.
Do not include any numeric values, targets, dates, or time horizons from any reference report; all values must be generated from the new entity’s data.
quality_checks_for_generation: IFRS anchoring check: Section includes an IFRS S1/S2 basis statement and clearly separates general sustainability vs climate-related metrics.
Completeness check: Every disclosed metric includes definition, boundary notes (where relevant), reporting-period value/status, and target information (if applicable).
Traceability check: Every metric includes an external framework/source type (if applicable), an internal source location descriptor, and a mapping to the relevant report section/pillar.
No blanks check: Missing or inapplicable data are explicitly labeled with standardized status statements and brief reason categories.
Consistency check: Units, terminology, category taxonomies, and formatting are consistent across pages and between narrative and tables.
Comparability check: Any methodology/definition changes are disclosed with a comparability impact note and treatment of prior-period information (if presented).
Audit-readiness check: Methodologies are described with clear steps, assumptions, and edge-case rules; footnotes are used appropriately and are cross-referenced.
Assurance separation check: Assurance statements are clearly separated from descriptive reporting; assurance markers (if used) have a single consolidated legend and scope/limitations note.
Navigation check: Multi-page tables repeat headers; section headers/footers support orientation; mapping column enables readers to find related narrative.
Safety check: Output contains no organization-specific names, people, committees, vendors, tools, locations, awards, achievements, or copied phrasing from any reference report.
